meta.title: Plug Power — Andy Marsh's vertically-integrated hydrogen fuel-cell platform through the materials-handling base and the green-hydrogen production pivot
meta.abstract: Plug Power is a Latham, New York-based hydrogen fuel-cell and electrolyser company that has built its commercial base on the GenDrive proton-exchange-membrane fuel-cell system for industrial material-handling trucks (forklifts), with anchor customers Amazon and Walmart driving the substantial early-stage commercial volume. Under CEO Andy Marsh (since 2008), the company executed the strategic expansion through the 2020-2021 acquisitions of Giner ELX (electrolyser systems), United Hydrogen Group (liquid hydrogen production), and other smaller targets, plus the announced strategic partnerships with Renault, SK Group, and Acciona. The 2021-2024 period was defined by the substantial capital raises supporting the green hydrogen production network build-out at Georgia, Tennessee, Louisiana, New York, and other US locations, plus the operational and accounting challenges that culminated in the 2024 going-concern warning and the subsequent operational restructuring. The current strategic posture combines the legacy materials-handling fuel-cell business with the emerging green hydrogen production network, the stationary fuel-cell systems for data centre and broader backup-power applications (including AI data centre opportunities), and the broader hydrogen ecosystem positioning. Under CFO Paul Middleton and the broader executive team, the operational restructuring through 2024-2025 has focused on cost-base reduction, working capital efficiency, and the broader capital structure stabilisation against the continuing green hydrogen production network execution.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## Company at a Glance

Plug Power Inc. (NASDAQ: PLUG) entered the frozen window on very different terms from those that had defined the 2024 panic. By March 2026 the company’s principal executive office was at 125 Vista Boulevard in Slingerlands, New York, Jose Luis Crespo had succeeded Andy Marsh as chief executive, and Marsh had moved to non-executive chairman. The shift mattered because the company Crespo inherited was no longer selling a simple top-line-growth story; it was trying to prove that a hydrogen platform assembled in the capital-markets boom could now be run as a disciplined industrial business. [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm) [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx)

Plug still had scale that many hydrogen peers lacked. In March 2026 it said it had deployed more than 74,000 fuel-cell systems worldwide, operated at more than 280 hydrogen-powered material-handling sites, and run hydrogen-production assets in Georgia, Tennessee and Louisiana. Its first-quarter 2026 update also pointed to more than 320 MW of electrolyzer capacity deployed globally. That made Plug less a single-product vendor than a stack of connected businesses: warehouse fuel cells, stationary backup power, electrolysers, hydrogen logistics and owned production. [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The operating detail in the May 2026 release was equally important. Management said GenDrive per-unit quarterly service costs were down more than 30 per cent year on year, hydrogen fuel sales were up 22 per cent and the hydrogen fuel margin rate had improved by 54 percentage points. Those were still early-stage turnaround numbers rather than proof of a settled margin structure, but they showed that the installed base and the production network were beginning to work together in the way Plug had long promised. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## Financial Baseline

The revenue line had also moved on. Plug reported net revenue of $891.3 million in 2023, $628.8 million in 2024 and $709.9 million in 2025. First-quarter 2026 revenue then rose 22 per cent year on year to $163.5 million. The key point was not simply that 2025 had improved on 2024; it was that the supposed information gap had already closed within the frozen window and showed a business that had stabilised, if not yet normalised. [2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000155837025002049/plug-20241231x10k.htm) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

| Fiscal year | Net revenue (USD mn) |
| --- | ---: |
| 2023 | 891.3 |
| 2024 | 628.8 |
| 2025 | 709.9 |

## From Going Concern to Managed Liquidity

The March 2024 going-concern disclosure remained the hinge of the modern Plug story, but by the 2025 annual report the emergency language had been replaced by a conventional liquidity discussion. The 2025 10-K said working capital was $799.7 million at December 31, 2025, including $368.5 million of unrestricted cash and $186.7 million of current restricted cash. The March 2026 quarter then showed total cash above $802 million, of which $223.2 million was unrestricted and roughly $578.8 million restricted. The balance sheet was still burdened by losses, convertible debt and finance obligations, but the immediate solvency crisis described in early 2024 had passed. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## DOE Loan and the Data-Centre Turn

The federal-financing story also needed updating. By the frozen date the Department of Energy facility was not merely a May 2024 conditional commitment; Plug had closed a loan guarantee of up to $1.66 billion on January 16, 2025. But the 2025 annual report then disclosed that the company suspended activities related to the DOE loan programme on November 7, 2025 and recorded a $13.2 million charge for capitalised closing fees. That sequence did not erase the importance of federal support, but it did change the tenor of the capital story from one of pending large-scale project debt to one of selective redeployment and balance-sheet triage. [DOE closing release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Closes-Loan-Guarantee-from-the-U.S.-Department-of-Energy/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

The adjacent data-centre narrative had also become more concrete than the old “prospective AI backup power” wording suggested. In November 2025 Plug said it had signed a non-binding letter of intent to monetise electricity rights in New York and one other location and collaborate with a US data-centre developer. In February 2026 it followed with a definitive agreement with Stream Data Centers to sell its Project Gateway site in New York for at least $132.5 million, the first step in a broader $275 million infrastructure-optimisation plan. What the disclosures supported was a real data-centre land-and-power monetisation pathway and a real commercial relationship; what they did not yet show was a disclosed megawatt-scale fuel-cell order. [November 2025 infrastructure release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-to-Generate-Over-275-Million-Through-Monetization-of-Electricity-Rights-and-Operational-Efficiencies-Supports-Major-U-S--Data-Center-Build-Out/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

## What the Snapshot Actually Showed

By May 23, 2026, Plug looked neither like the terminally impaired company implied by the March 2024 panic nor like the frictionless hydrogen champion imagined during the 2021 capital boom. It was a re-cut industrial platform with a new chief executive, a still-large installed base, a hydrogen network that was finally operational across three southern sites, and a capital plan that leaned as much on asset monetisation and operating discipline as on fresh federal debt. The open question had narrowed: not whether Plug would survive the next year, but whether improving equipment mix, better hydrogen sourcing and lower capital intensity could finally convert scale into durable profitability. [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

chapters.title: From 1997 founding through Marsh era, anchor customers, and going-concern restoration
chapters.body:
## The Joint-Venture Origin, 1997–2008

Plug Power’s corporate shell predated its current hydrogen narrative by decades. The company said in older SEC filings that it was organised in Delaware on June 27, 1997, was originally a joint venture between Edison Development Corporation and Mechanical Technology Incorporated, and became listed on Nasdaq on October 29, 1999. The founding proposition was broad fuel-cell commercialisation, not the warehouse-specialist identity that later defined the group. [historical 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000100329709000075/esplugpower10k.htm)

The first decade as a public company produced more engineering effort than commercial proof. Plug cycled through residential and stationary-power ideas before settling on a market where fuel cells solved an immediate operational problem rather than an aspirational decarbonisation problem. That is why Andy Marsh’s arrival in April 2008 mattered so much: the board brought in a telecom-power operator rather than a laboratory evangelist. The 8-K announcing his appointment said Marsh had built Valere Power from start-up to a company with more than 200 employees and $90 million of revenue before selling it in 2007. [Marsh appointment](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2008/PLUG-POWER-NAMES-ANDREW-MARSH-PRESIDENT-AND-CHIEF-EXECUTIVE-OFFICER-EFFECTIVE-APRIL-8-2008-2008-4-7/default.aspx)

The commercial reset that followed was as much about discipline as technology. Marsh did not invent PEM fuel cells at Plug; he chose the first application where they could win on throughput and labour economics before any broad hydrogen economy existed. That was the cultural pivot that separated the later Plug from the capital-consuming development-stage company described in older SEC filings. [historical 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000100329709000075/esplugpower10k.htm) [Marsh appointment](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2008/PLUG-POWER-NAMES-ANDREW-MARSH-PRESIDENT-AND-CHIEF-EXECUTIVE-OFFICER-EFFECTIVE-APRIL-8-2008-2008-4-7/default.aspx)

## The Warehouse Pivot

Marsh’s crucial move was to narrow Plug’s commercial ambition to material handling. The company’s GenDrive systems could replace lead-acid batteries in forklifts operating through multiple warehouse shifts, where battery swapping consumed labour, floor space and time. A 2014 company release tied that strategy to a multi-site GenKey order from Walmart, then described as Plug’s largest order to date. That was the operating template that made the later hydrogen-platform strategy possible: sell productivity first, then build fuel, service and infrastructure around the installed base. [Walmart multi-site order](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2014/Plug-Power-Receives-Multi-Site-GenKey-Order-2014-2-10/default.aspx)

The customer-capital-markets architecture that later shaped reported revenue crystallised in 2017. Plug’s 2025 annual report said the Amazon transaction agreement and related warrant were signed on April 4, 2017, and the Walmart warrant transaction agreement followed on July 20, 2017. Walmart had already been an important operating customer before that; what changed in 2017 was that both relationships were embedded directly into the equity structure through warrants tied to commercial purchases. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Walmart expanded collaboration](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2017/Plug-Power-Announces-Expanded-Collaboration-With-Walmart-2017-7-21/default.aspx)

That structure brought blue-chip validation and a reporting complication that endured for years. Because the customer warrants were treated as reductions of revenue, Plug’s reported sales could no longer be read naively as a clean proxy for hardware demand. The commercial success of the Amazon and Walmart roll-outs therefore strengthened the operating story even as it made the accounting story harder to parse. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Restatement completion](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Restatement-of-Previously-Issued-Financial-Statements-and-Files-2020-Annual-Report-2021-5-14/default.aspx)

## The Restatement and the Capital Boom

Those customer warrants eventually became an accounting problem as well as a commercial advantage. Plug announced in March 2021 that it would restate previously issued financial statements for fiscal years 2018 and 2019 and quarterly filings for 2019 and 2020. It completed that process in May 2021 when it filed its 2020 annual report, describing the affected periods as the “restated periods”. The episode was therefore a 2021 restatement covering multiple earlier periods, not a one-off 2019 event. [Restatement announcement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-to-Restate-Previously-Issued-Financial-Statements-2021-3-16/default.aspx) [Restatement completion](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Restatement-of-Previously-Issued-Financial-Statements-and-Files-2020-Annual-Report-2021-5-14/default.aspx)

The restatement coincided with the moment when capital was cheapest. Plug raised approximately $1 billion in November 2020, then completed a $2 billion-plus common-stock raise in January 2021, then closed SK Group’s $1.6 billion strategic investment in February 2021. Together the three headline transactions amounted to more than $4.5 billion of gross capital in roughly four months. That cash financed the most ambitious expansion in the company’s history. [November 2020 equity raise](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Raises-Approximately-1B-to-Accelerate-the-First-Nation-Wide-Green-Hydrogen-Network-2020-11-24/default.aspx) [January 2021 raise](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Powers-2B-Capital-Raise-Marks-the-Largest-Bought-Deal-in-the-CleanTech-Sector-2021-2-9/default.aspx) [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx)

In practical terms, the money underwrote several bets at once: owned hydrogen production in Georgia, Tennessee, Louisiana and New York; a larger electrolyser manufacturing footprint; international joint ventures; cryogenic logistics; and a broader sales push across mobility and stationary power. The financing window was so generous that Plug could try to build an ecosystem rather than a product company. The later crisis was, in part, the bill arriving for that ambition. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx) [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx) [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx) [Applied Cryo](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Acquisition-of-Applied-Cryo-Technologies-2021-11-23/default.aspx)

## Vertical Integration Became the Strategy

Plug had already started the pivot toward vertical integration before the biggest equity cheques arrived. On June 23, 2020 it completed the acquisitions of United Hydrogen and Giner ELX, bringing hydrogen production, liquefaction, distribution and PEM-electrolyser capability closer to the centre of the company. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx)

The 2021 expansion then broadened into partnerships and additional acquisitions. Plug and Renault unveiled the Hyvia joint venture in June 2021 to build a hydrogen light-commercial-vehicle ecosystem in Europe. Plug and Acciona Energía finalised AccionaPlug in November 2021 as a 50-50 Iberian hydrogen venture headquartered in Madrid. Plug also completed the purchase of Applied Cryo Technologies in November 2021 and said in its fourth-quarter 2021 shareholder letter that it had completed the acquisition of Frames Group in the fourth quarter. The cumulative result was a company trying to own not only the fuel-cell stack, but also the fuel molecule, the cryogenic logistics and the project-engineering layer around large installations. [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx) [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx) [Applied Cryo](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Acquisition-of-Applied-Cryo-Technologies-2021-11-23/default.aspx) [Q4 2021 shareholder letter](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/files/doc_financials/2021/q4/4Q21-investor-letter.pdf)

## From Going Concern to Succession

The 2021 build-out proved vastly easier to finance than to operationalise. By March 2024 Plug disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern, then spent the next year shrinking working capital needs, reducing cost and renegotiating the cadence of its network build-out. In May 2024 the DOE Loan Programs Office announced a conditional commitment for up to $1.66 billion, and in January 2025 Plug said it had closed the loan guarantee. But the 2025 10-K later recorded a November 7, 2025 suspension of DOE-loan activities and a $13.2 million write-off of capitalised closing fees, which showed how quickly the company’s capital plan had changed even after a headline federal win. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [DOE closing release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Closes-Loan-Guarantee-from-the-U.S.-Department-of-Energy/default.aspx)

The late-2025 and early-2026 infrastructure monetisation announcements completed the turn in tone. Instead of talking only about building more hydrogen assets, Plug described a plan to generate more than $275 million from electricity-rights monetisation, restricted-cash release and lower maintenance expense, then signed the Stream Data Centers agreement around Project Gateway. History had moved from expansion to portfolio triage. [November 2025 infrastructure release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-to-Generate-Over-275-Million-Through-Monetization-of-Electricity-Rights-and-Operational-Efficiencies-Supports-Major-U-S--Data-Center-Build-Out/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

Leadership changed in the middle of that reset. Plug announced in October 2025 that Jose Luis Crespo would become president immediately and chief executive upon the filing of the 2025 10-K. On March 3, 2026 the company confirmed that Crespo had assumed the chief executive role on March 2 and that Marsh had moved to chairman. Corporate history therefore no longer ended with a Marsh-led operating recovery; by the frozen date it had already become a succession story in which the founder-era public-company survivor handed the restructuring’s second phase to a long-time internal operator. [Incoming CEO announcement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-Names-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Incoming-CEO-to-Succeed-Long-Term-Leader-Andy-Marsh/default.aspx) [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx)

Crespo’s inheritance was more concrete than a generic “next phase” handoff. The same March 2026 release that confirmed the succession also pointed to more than $700 million of 2025 revenue, over 74,000 deployed fuel-cell systems and a strategy now framed around operational discipline, capital efficiency and profitable growth rather than unchecked scale. The company history through the frozen date therefore closed on a managerial change that mirrored the business-model change beneath it. [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [FY2025 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx)

chapters.title: GenDrive, stationary fuel cells, electrolysers, hydrogen production network
chapters.body:
## GenDrive: The Base Business

Plug’s modern business was still built on forklifts. GenDrive remained the installed-base engine that justified almost everything else on the balance sheet: hydrogen sourcing, service contracts, fuelling infrastructure and a large share of the company’s manufacturing footprint. Walmart was the first large multi-site GenKey proof point in 2014; the Amazon and Walmart warrant structures that later affected reported revenue were both 2017 contracts. By March 2026 Plug said it had deployed more than 74,000 fuel-cell systems at more than 280 hydrogen-powered material-handling sites worldwide. [Walmart multi-site order](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2014/Plug-Power-Receives-Multi-Site-GenKey-Order-2014-2-10/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx)

GenDrive’s appeal was never ideological. It came from fast refuelling, steady power output through long shifts and the removal of battery-changing infrastructure from warehouse floors. That made the product unusually sticky with high-throughput operators once a site had already been converted, which helps explain why the March 2026 and May 2026 updates still emphasised expansion with existing customer sites, including Amazon and Walmart, rather than a wholesale reinvention of the addressable market. [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## GenFuel: The Infrastructure Layer

The installed base mattered because Plug did not stop at selling the power unit. Its materials-handling proposition bundled fuelling, service and hydrogen supply in a way that turned a forklift conversion into a long-duration operating relationship. The economic reward for that design was recurring revenue; the risk was that Plug carried the burden of fuel sourcing and site infrastructure when hydrogen costs moved against it. That is why the company’s own production network later became so important to the segment story. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## GenSure and Stationary Power

Plug’s stationary-power line, GenSure, had long existed at the edge of the investment case. Through the frozen window it remained primarily a backup-power rather than baseload-power proposition, which distinguished it from Bloom Energy’s always-on server architecture. The product’s legacy markets were telecommunications and other critical facilities where diesel alternatives could justify a premium if uptime and emissions mattered enough. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

What changed after 2024 was not that Plug disclosed a giant booked order in AI infrastructure; it was that the company began tying real land, power and liquidity actions to the data-centre build-out. In November 2025 it said it would monetise electricity rights and collaborate with a US data-centre developer. In February 2026 it named Stream Data Centers as the buyer of Project Gateway in New York. That sequence suggested Plug was trying to turn a hydrogen-site development asset into a data-centre and power-platform opportunity, while still preserving optionality for fuel-cell backup solutions. [November 2025 infrastructure release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-to-Generate-Over-275-Million-Through-Monetization-of-Electricity-Rights-and-Operational-Efficiencies-Supports-Major-U-S--Data-Center-Build-Out/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

## Electrolysers: The Giner ELX Platform

Plug’s electrolyser business came in-house with the June 2020 acquisition of Giner ELX. Giner ELX gave Plug a PEM-electrolyser stack platform, engineering talent and a product line that could be sold to third parties as well as used inside Plug’s own hydrogen plants. By the first quarter of 2026 Plug was describing more than 320 MW of electrolyzer capacity deployed globally, alongside named projects including a 100 MW system with Galp Energia in Portugal and a 25 MW project with Iberdrola and BP in Spain. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The commercial implication was that the electrolyser business had become more than an internal-transfer mechanism. Plug’s March 2026 results release called 2025 a record $187 million revenue year for electrolysers and pointed to an approximate $8 billion global sales funnel. That did not remove execution risk, but it did mean the segment could no longer be treated simply as captive kit for company-owned hydrogen plants. [FY2025 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx)

The dual role remained important. Plug’s own hydrogen plants were proof sites for the technology, while third-party projects provided a route to revenue that did not depend on Plug financing every production asset itself. In theory that gave the segment more resilience than the early “build our own network first” strategy had implied. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

| Segment | Frozen-window proof point |
| --- | --- |
| GenDrive / material handling | 74,000+ deployed fuel-cell systems; 280+ hydrogen-powered sites |
| GenSure / stationary power | Data-centre collaboration and Project Gateway monetisation trail |
| GenEco electrolyzers | 320+ MW deployed globally; $187m electrolyzer revenue in 2025 |
| Hydrogen production | Georgia, Tennessee and Louisiana operating at about 40 TPD combined |

[CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [FY2025 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

## The Hydrogen Production Network

The company’s most capital-intensive segment was the production network designed to reduce dependence on third-party merchant hydrogen. By the frozen window the operational map had moved materially:

| Site | Disclosure-supported status by May 23, 2026 |
| --- | --- |
| Woodbine, Georgia | Started liquid green hydrogen production in January 2024; designed for 15 TPD |
| Charleston, Tennessee | Restarted in February 2024; added about 10 TPD |
| St. Gabriel, Louisiana | Commissioned in April 2025 through the Hidrogenii joint venture; 15 TPD liquefaction plant |
| Project Gateway, New York | Subject of February 2026 sale agreement with Stream Data Centers |

[Georgia start-up](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2024/Plug-Power-Starts-Production-of-Liquid-Green-Hydrogen-at-its-Georgia-Plant/default.aspx) [Tennessee restart](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2024/Plug-Power-Starts-Production-of-Liquid-Hydrogen-at-its-Existing-Tennessee-Plant/default.aspx) [Louisiana commissioning](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Hidrogenii-a-Plug-and-Olin-Joint-VentureCommissions-15-Ton-Per-Day-Hydrogen-Liquefaction-Plant-in-Louisiana/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

That status table changed the interpretation of the network. Georgia, Tennessee and Louisiana were no longer future plants; they were disclosed as operating assets with combined capacity of about 40 tons per day. New York, by contrast, had become a monetisation candidate rather than an obvious next internal-production leg. In other words, Plug had not abandoned the hydrogen-network idea, but it had become more selective about which sites were there to produce hydrogen and which were there to release capital. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

The company’s own disclosures also made clear why this mattered operationally. Better fuel sourcing and greater leverage on the network were cited as drivers of the first-quarter 2026 margin improvement. That suggested the plant base had stopped being only a capex burden and had started to influence unit economics in the direction management had promised for several years. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## International Architecture

Plug’s segments also had an international outlet even where the financial contribution remained hard to isolate. Hyvia put fuel cells into the European light-commercial-vehicle conversation, AccionaPlug linked Plug’s technology to Iberian renewable power, and SK’s investment created an Asian commercial bridge. Those ventures were not the core of 2025 or first-quarter 2026 reported revenue, but they showed how management intended the same stack, electrolyser and hydrogen-supply capabilities to travel across geographies and applications. [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx) [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx) [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx)

## Segment Logic After the Reset

Read together, the segments showed why Plug had remained such a difficult company to analyse. GenDrive supplied the installed base and recurring customer touchpoints. GenSure represented a power-product adjacency whose commercial proof remained early. The Giner-derived electrolyser business gave Plug external equipment revenue as well as internal supply. The hydrogen-production network was meant to repair the margin damage caused by buying fuel from third parties. What changed by May 2026 was that management no longer described all four pieces as marching in lockstep toward the same giant build-out. Crespo inherited a model in which some assets were being scaled, some were being monetised and some were being asked to justify themselves on return rather than ambition. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The connective tissue across the segments remained the central fact of the company. A forklift deployment pulled through fuel service. Fuel service improved if the owned network supplied more of the molecule. The owned network in turn justified in-house electrolyser manufacturing and cryogenic logistics. That circularity was what bulls regarded as a moat and what bears regarded as an amplification mechanism for mistakes. By the frozen date both interpretations still had evidence behind them. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, operating losses, capital structure, and DOE loan
chapters.body:
## Revenue Growth Was Real; Profitability Was Not

Plug’s long financial arc still turned on a simple tension: real commercial growth had coexisted with a cost structure that repeatedly outran it. The 2025 annual report disclosed net revenue of $709.9 million for 2025, up from $628.8 million in 2024, but still below the $891.3 million peak reported for 2023. The 2025 results therefore showed a disclosed recovery year rather than an information gap. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [FY2025 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx)

| Year | Net revenue (USD mn) | Net loss (USD mn) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2023 | 891.3 | 1,396.0 |
| 2024 | 628.8 | 2,104.9 |
| 2025 | 709.9 | 1,693.7 |

[2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000155837025002049/plug-20241231x10k.htm) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

The top line also shifted by component. In 2025 Plug reported $371.1 million of equipment and related-infrastructure revenue, $94.5 million from services on fuel-cell systems and related infrastructure, $107.6 million from power-purchase agreements, and $133.4 million from fuel delivered to customers and related equipment. In 2024 those respective figures were $390.3 million, $52.2 million, $77.8 million and $97.9 million. The mix was becoming more service- and network-heavy at the same time as the company was trying to improve gross margin. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

The capital-structure cost of survival was also visible in the share count. Plug’s 2025 annual report showed 1,394,241,538 shares issued, including shares in treasury, at December 31, 2025 against 934,126,897 a year earlier. The first-quarter 2026 filing then showed 1,395,643,390 issued shares and a charter expanded to 3.0 billion authorised shares. That is the arithmetic beneath the company’s repeated equity dependence: the balance sheet had been stabilised in part by very substantial dilution. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The revenue composition also shifted in ways that made the topline harder to read casually. The 2025 10-K showed sales of equipment and related infrastructure falling to $371.1 million from $390.3 million in 2024 and $711.4 million in 2023, while services, power purchase agreements and fuel-delivery revenue all increased. Plug was becoming less dependent on one-time equipment revenue and more dependent on the economics of running a network. That was strategically logical, but it also made gross-margin improvement harder because the network was exactly where the company had suffered its worst historical losses. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

## The Cost of Building Too Much Too Early

The company’s losses were not the by-product of one bad quarter or one accounting distortion. They reflected a business that tried to do several capital-intensive things at once: manufacture fuel-cell systems, build a domestic hydrogen-generation footprint, support power-purchase contracts, and finance customer deployments. The 2024 annual report said net losses were approximately $724.0 million in 2022, $1.4 billion in 2023 and $2.1 billion in 2024; the 2025 annual report then recorded a still-enormous $1.69 billion net loss for 2025. Losses improved from the 2024 nadir but did not disappear merely because revenue recovered. [2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000155837025002049/plug-20241231x10k.htm) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

The segment data in the 2025 10-K showed where the strain had moved. Service-contract recovery, lower inventory write-downs and a better fuel-sourcing position helped. But the same filing also recorded $785.4 million of impairment in 2025 and a continuing drag from finance obligations, warrant liabilities and convertible instruments. This was no longer a simple “burn cash to grow” story; it was a partial recapitalisation taking place at the same time as an operating restructuring. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

Cash-flow detail reinforced the same point. Net cash used in operating activities improved to $535.8 million in 2025 from $728.6 million in 2024, while lower-of-cost-or-net-realisable-value inventory adjustments and excess-and-obsolete inventory charges fell to $97.1 million from $172.0 million. Those were real improvements, but they were improvements inside a company still consuming large amounts of cash and still carrying heavy clean-up charges from earlier overexpansion. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

| 2025 year-end metric | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Working capital | $799.7m |
| Unrestricted cash | $368.5m |
| Restricted cash | $625.4m |
| Total liabilities | $1.59bn |
| Convertible debt instruments | $431.0m |
| Finance obligations | $191.8m |
| Warrant liabilities | $52.3m |

[2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

## The 2020–2021 Capital Cycle

Management had financed the hydrogen build-out in a market that briefly tolerated almost any clean-tech ambition. Plug raised approximately $1 billion in November 2020, then completed a $2 billion-plus equity raise in January 2021, then closed SK Group’s $1.6 billion strategic investment in February 2021. That cash was enough to justify a network strategy that included hydrogen plants, electrolysers, cryogenic logistics and international partnerships. It was not enough to protect the company from the execution cost of trying to scale all of them at once. [November 2020 equity raise](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Raises-Approximately-1B-to-Accelerate-the-First-Nation-Wide-Green-Hydrogen-Network-2020-11-24/default.aspx) [January 2021 raise](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Powers-2B-Capital-Raise-Marks-the-Largest-Bought-Deal-in-the-CleanTech-Sector-2021-2-9/default.aspx) [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx)

A related complication was the customer-warrant accounting tied to Amazon and Walmart. The contra-revenue treatment did not create the underlying cash burn, but it did distort the cleanness of reported revenue comparisons and contributed to the 2021 restatement. That is why the financial story could not be read only through the revenue line: some of the headline growth years were simultaneously years of accounting clean-up, capital abundance and worsening unit economics. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Restatement completion](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Restatement-of-Previously-Issued-Financial-Statements-and-Files-2020-Annual-Report-2021-5-14/default.aspx)

## 2024 Was the Break Point

The March 2024 going-concern disclosure forced Plug to stop pretending that every booked revenue dollar was equally valuable. Through 2024 the company cut headcount, consolidated facilities, reduced capital spending and reworked supplier relationships under the Project Quantum Leap banner. The March 2025 year-end update said fourth-quarter 2024 revenue was $191.5 million and described better operating cash flow, lower capital expenditure and a targeted $150 million to $200 million of annual expense reduction. That made the 2024 revenue decline analytically important: it was not merely weaker demand, but the financial consequence of abandoning activities that were proving too expensive to support. [2024 results update](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx) [March 2025 update](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx)

## DOE, Restricted Cash and the New Liquidity Equation

By May 2026 the harder question around the DOE loan was not whether it had closed, but how much of the original plan still mattered. Plug closed the DOE guarantee in January 2025, then disclosed in the 2025 10-K that it suspended DOE-loan activities in November 2025 and wrote off $13.2 million of capitalised closing fees. At the same time, the company had assembled other forms of liquidity: year-end 2025 unrestricted cash of $368.5 million, restricted cash of $625.4 million, and a May 2026 update saying roughly $50 million of restricted cash was expected to release per quarter over the next few years. [DOE closing release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Closes-Loan-Guarantee-from-the-U.S.-Department-of-Energy/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The capital structure itself remained complicated. As of year-end 2025 Plug had $431.0 million of convertible debt instruments measured at fair value, $191.8 million of finance obligations, $52.3 million of warrant liabilities and total liabilities of $1.59 billion. The first quarter of 2026 then showed stockholders’ equity of $749.8 million and total liabilities of $1.59 billion, illustrating how far the company still was from a plain-vanilla industrial balance sheet. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

First-quarter 2026 results sharpened the picture further. Revenue rose to $163.5 million from $133.7 million a year earlier, gross margin improved materially, and cash usage was described as modestly better than internal plan. But the same release still framed asset monetisation, including the Stream transaction and a targeted sale of Louisiana investment tax credits, as important ingredients in funding the path to positive EBITDAS by the fourth quarter of 2026. Plug had therefore not solved the capital problem outright; it had replaced one funding mix with another. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

The quarter’s margin details explained why management thought the target was still reachable. Plug said first-quarter 2026 GAAP gross margin improved to negative 13 per cent from negative 55 per cent a year earlier, while improved service execution, pricing, network leverage and lower third-party fuel sourcing helped narrow the gap. The business was still lossmaking, but the direction of travel had become visible in reported metrics rather than conference-call aspiration alone. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## What the Financial Story Became

The company’s financial story by the frozen date was no longer “raise equity, build everything, wait for hydrogen demand”. It had become a harder and more conventional industrial turnaround: protect liquidity, shrink the fixed-cost base, extract better margins from the installed network, and monetise non-core infrastructure while preserving the hydrogen platform’s strategic spine. The improvement from 2024 to 2025 was real. So was the distance still left to travel. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

chapters.title: Post-2014 quarters through 2020-2021 capital raises and going-concern restoration
chapters.body:
## Capital Structure Transformation, 2020–2021

The warrant accounting complications of the anchor-customer period (see Corporate History) were resolved through the 2021 restatement, which also exposed a material weakness in internal controls that required remediation. The restated periods reset the baseline from which the subsequent capital raise cycle would launch.

## Revenue Ramp and the Limits of Capital

The revenue trajectory validated the deployment model, reflecting an expanding product mix as electrolyser sales, hydrogen production services, and stationary power deployments supplemented the core GenDrive business.

The acquisition programme — United Hydrogen, Giner ELX, Frames Group, Applied Cryo Technologies — added the vertical integration capabilities required for an integrated green hydrogen value chain.

The operating losses, however, scaled in parallel. Green hydrogen production is capital-intensive at construction and operating-cost-intensive at volume, particularly when the company is simultaneously building out multiple facilities, scaling manufacturing operations, and absorbing acquired businesses that carry their own integration costs. The gross margin performance on hydrogen fuel — where Plug Power was supplying material-handling customers under long-term contracts that fixed pricing while its own production costs remained elevated — compressed operating results through the 2022 and 2023 periods in ways that the revenue growth line alone did not fully communicate.

## March 2024: The Going-Concern Disclosure

The formal going-concern disclosure with the fiscal year 2023 results reflected a cash consumption rate that had outpaced the capital structure the 2020–2021 raises had provided. The stock, which had traded above $70 in January 2021, was by March 2024 trading in single digits — the market was not disposed to credit the capital-intensive infrastructure network at prior valuation levels.

## The DOE Loan Guarantee and Operational Restructuring

The May 2024 DOE conditional commitment provided the pivotal stabilisation mechanism. The operational restructuring produced deliberate revenue compression — from $891 million to $629 million — as the company prioritised margin improvement over volume growth. By year-end 2024, the going-concern qualification had been resolved through the combination of DOE commitment, restructuring, and supplemental capital actions.

chapters.title: Marsh, Middleton CFO, Crespo COO, and the Schoeppner-chaired board
chapters.body:
## The Marsh-to-Crespo Handover

Plug’s 2026 proxy and March 2026 transition release said Jose Luis Crespo became chief executive on March 2, 2026 after first being appointed president in October 2025, while Andy Marsh moved from chief executive to non-executive chairman. [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm) [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [Incoming CEO announcement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-Names-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Incoming-CEO-to-Succeed-Long-Term-Leader-Andy-Marsh/default.aspx)

Marsh nevertheless remained the defining management figure in Plug’s corporate history. The company’s April 2008 appointment filing said he had arrived from Valere Power with a telecom-power operating background and had been brought in specifically to commercialise rather than merely develop the technology. Eighteen years later he was still the bridge between Plug’s speculative early years and its scaled hydrogen-platform ambitions, but he was no longer the executive running day-to-day operations. [Marsh appointment](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2008/PLUG-POWER-NAMES-ANDREW-MARSH-PRESIDENT-AND-CHIEF-EXECUTIVE-OFFICER-EFFECTIVE-APRIL-8-2008-2008-4-7/default.aspx) [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm)

## The Operating Bench

The executive bench under Crespo included Paul B. Middleton as chief financial officer, chief accounting officer and executive vice-president; Dean C. Fullerton as chief operating officer; and Benjamin Haycraft as chief strategy officer and general manager for EMEA. Fullerton had been hired from Amazon in 2024, and Haycraft held the strategy portfolio in the company’s current public materials by the frozen date. [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm) [COO appointment](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2024/Plug-Power-Names-Amazon-Executive-as-its-New-COO/default.aspx) [Leadership page](https://www.plugpower.com/about-us/leadership/) [Haycraft profile](https://www.plugpower.com/dvteam/benjamin-haycraft/)

Middleton’s role deserved emphasis because he had become the continuity finance executive through both the 2021 capital boom and the 2024 liquidity crisis. Plug’s own leadership page said he joined as chief financial officer in 2014. That meant the two practical centres of gravity during the turnaround were no longer Marsh and a speculative board configuration, but Crespo on commercial execution and Middleton on balance-sheet management. [Leadership page](https://www.plugpower.com/about-us/leadership/)

## The Board as Actually Disclosed

The 2026 proxy showed a board built around Marsh, Crespo and longstanding independent directors including George C. McNamee, Maureen O. Helmer, Gregory L. Kenausis, Kavita Mahtani, Colin Angle, Mark J. Bonney, Patrick Joggerst and Gary K. Willis. It was a continuity board managing a leadership succession and a balance-sheet reset rather than a freshly assembled thematic board for a single financing event. [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926052851/tm263044-1_def14a.htm)

## What Leadership Meant by May 2026

Crespo’s rise was not an outsider rescue narrative. Plug’s March 2026 release said he had spent more than 12 years at the company, most recently as president and chief revenue officer, and had helped grow revenue from roughly $27 million in 2013 to more than $700 million in 2025. The succession therefore preserved strategic continuity while changing the operating emphasis: less founder-style evangelism, more commercial and margin discipline. That matched the company’s broader turn from expansion-at-all-costs toward execution, cash control and selective asset monetisation. [CEO transition](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Welcomes-Jose-Luis-Crespo-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [FY2025 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-with-Strong-Sales-Growth-and-Margin-Expansion/default.aspx)

chapters.title: Amazon, Walmart, Renault, SK Group, Acciona, and the hydrogen value chain
chapters.body:
## The Anchor-Customer Architecture

Plug’s commercial history was shaped by a small number of customers large enough to influence both operations and the balance sheet. Walmart was the early operating proof point: in February 2014 Plug announced a multi-site GenKey order covering six Walmart distribution centres over two years. Amazon became the more consequential capital-markets customer later, when the 2025 annual report said Plug signed the Amazon transaction agreement and warrant on April 4, 2017. Walmart’s warrant-bearing transaction followed on July 20, 2017. [Walmart multi-site order](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2014/Plug-Power-Receives-Multi-Site-GenKey-Order-2014-2-10/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Walmart expanded collaboration](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2017/Plug-Power-Announces-Expanded-Collaboration-With-Walmart-2017-7-21/default.aspx)

By the frozen date both companies still mattered. Plug’s first-quarter 2026 release cited expansion with existing customer sites, including Amazon and Walmart, and highlighted better service economics in material handling. The relationship had matured from “prove the technology” to “improve the unit economics at an already-established installed base”. [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

Their importance went beyond volume. Amazon and Walmart were the customers that made Plug’s revenue accounting, capital raising and investor communications inseparable from one another. When management later talked about better fuel economics, service-cost reductions or improved warrant charges, it was still, in substantial part, talking about how the anchor-customer base behaved. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## Renault, Hyvia and the European Vehicle Bet

The Renault relationship sat in a different category. Hyvia, launched in June 2021 as a 50-50 joint venture between Renault Group and Plug, was meant to create a full hydrogen light-commercial-vehicle ecosystem in Europe rather than simply sell Plug hardware into an existing fleet. The venture talked not only about vans, but also green hydrogen and refuelling stations. That made Hyvia strategically important even if it had not yet become material enough to dominate Plug’s disclosed revenue profile. [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx)

Hyvia also illustrated how Plug wanted to export its domestic template. Rather than remain a component supplier, it tried to pair vehicles, hydrogen supply and refuelling into a bundled ecosystem. The logic was familiar from warehouses; the geography and application were new. [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx)

## SK Group and Acciona

SK Group’s February 2021 $1.6 billion strategic investment was both financing and distribution strategy. It paired Plug with a Korean industrial group that could help carry the hydrogen pitch into Asian markets. The relationship later broadened into a formal joint-venture structure with SK E&S. The significance for this dossier was less near-term revenue than the fact that Plug repeatedly solved go-to-market challenges by partnering with incumbents that already had capital, regulatory relationships or customer access. [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx)

The same logic governed AccionaPlug. Plug and Acciona Energía finalised the 50-50 Iberian venture in November 2021, said it would be headquartered in Madrid, and named Alan Ripa as chief executive of the joint venture. [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx)

In both cases the partnerships served as substitutes for a global balance sheet Plug did not have. SK supplied capital and market access in Asia. Acciona supplied a renewables-heavy Iberian platform where green hydrogen economics could plausibly improve faster than in less advantaged power markets. [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx) [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx)

| Relationship | What Plug got |
| --- | --- |
| Walmart | Early multi-site operating proof, later warrant-linked commercial scale |
| Amazon | Large installed-base customer and the most consequential warrant structure |
| Renault / Hyvia | European vehicle platform and route to a bundled hydrogen LCV offer |
| SK Group | Capital plus Asian market access |
| Acciona Energía | Iberian renewable-power partner and local project vehicle |

[Walmart multi-site order](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2014/Plug-Power-Receives-Multi-Site-GenKey-Order-2014-2-10/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Hyvia launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/HYVIA-Renault-Group-and-Plug-Powers-Joint-Venture-Leads-the-Way-to-a-Complete-Ecosystem-of-Fuel-Cell-Powered-LCVs-Green-Hydrogen-and-Refueling-Stations-Across-Europe-2021-6-3/default.aspx) [SK closing](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-SK-Group-Complete-1.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-to-Build-Hydrogen-Economy-in-Asian-Markets-2021-2-25/default.aspx) [AccionaPlug launch](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-and-ACCIONA-Energa-Launch-AccionaPlug-to-Address-Green-Hydrogen-Market-in-Spain-and-Portugal-2021-11-30/default.aspx)

## The Logistics Layer

On the supply-chain side, Plug tried to reduce dependency not by vertically integrating every raw material, but by buying critical logistics and engineering capabilities. The June 2020 United Hydrogen and Giner ELX transaction added hydrogen generation, liquefaction and PEM-electrolyser capability. The November 2021 acquisition of Applied Cryo Technologies added cryogenic transportation, storage and hydrogen mobility fuelling equipment. Plug’s fourth-quarter 2021 shareholder letter then said the company had completed the acquisition of Frames Group during that same quarter, reinforcing the engineering-systems layer around larger hydrogen projects. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx) [Applied Cryo](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Acquisition-of-Applied-Cryo-Technologies-2021-11-23/default.aspx) [Q4 2021 shareholder letter](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/files/doc_financials/2021/q4/4Q21-investor-letter.pdf)

That strategy did not eliminate upstream exposure, but it changed where Plug was vulnerable. The company still depended on a specialised supply chain for stacks, membranes, catalysts, power electronics and plant equipment. What it increasingly controlled itself was the ability to move hydrogen through the system once it had been made: trailers, storage, fuelling equipment, liquefaction interfaces and project infrastructure. [Applied Cryo](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2021/Plug-Power-Completes-Acquisition-of-Applied-Cryo-Technologies-2021-11-23/default.aspx) [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

The merchant-hydrogen dependence that had hurt margins in earlier years is what made those logistics assets matter. So long as Plug had to buy too much hydrogen from third parties, the commercial value of the customer base did not cleanly translate into gross profit. The supply-chain build-out was therefore not a side story to the customer story; it was management’s attempt to repair the economics of serving those same customers. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

The logic can be stated another way: customer concentration was only tolerable if Plug could improve the margin earned on concentrated demand. The company’s own plants, cryogenic fleet and engineering stack were the instruments through which it tried to do that. Without them, Amazon and Walmart would have remained commercially impressive but economically frustrating accounts. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## Data Centres as a New Customer Category

The most interesting new customer category by the frozen date was not a retailer or an industrial gas buyer but the data-centre developer. Plug’s November 2025 release said it had signed a non-binding letter of intent to monetise electricity rights and collaborate with a US data-centre developer. The February 2026 Stream agreement then named the counterparty for Project Gateway in New York and set gross proceeds at at least $132.5 million, with total proceeds of up to $142 million depending on timing and asset-removal conditions. That did not yet prove that Plug had won a fleet of hyperscale fuel-cell deployments, but it did prove that the company’s customer map had expanded from forklifts and industrial partners into land, power and infrastructure negotiations with the data-centre build-out. [November 2025 infrastructure release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-to-Generate-Over-275-Million-Through-Monetization-of-Electricity-Rights-and-Operational-Efficiencies-Supports-Major-U-S--Data-Center-Build-Out/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

## The Commercial Shape of the Ecosystem

Read together, Plug’s customer and supply-chain architecture looked less like a broad consumer franchise than a chain of carefully chosen industrial relationships. Walmart helped validate multi-site material handling. Amazon and Walmart together shaped the warrant-accounting era. Renault, SK and Acciona carried Plug into geographies and applications it could not have entered cheaply on its own. Applied Cryo, United Hydrogen, Giner ELX and Frames helped move the company from selling devices to trying to control a hydrogen workflow. That ecosystem was the company’s most distinctive commercial asset by May 2026. It was also the reason the business remained so capital-intensive when execution slipped. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

chapters.title: Where Plug sits against Bloom, FuelCell Energy, Ballard, and electrolyser pure-plays
chapters.body:
## The Peer Map Changed

Plug still occupied an unusual position in the hydrogen sector by May 2026: more vertically integrated than most listed peers, but also more financially exposed to the cost of making that integration work. A proper comparison had to separate four arenas: stationary power, utility-scale and niche stationary fuel cells, heavy-duty motive power, and the broader electrolyser-and-hydrogen-infrastructure contest. [2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm)

## Bloom Energy: The Most Important Stationary Comparator

Bloom was the clearest comparator in stationary power and the most relevant reference point for the data-centre debate. Bloom itself reported $1.33 billion of revenue for 2023 and $2.02 billion for 2025. More importantly, it was already telling investors in February 2026 that full-year growth had been driven significantly by the AI data-centre industry. That put Bloom on firmer commercial ground than Plug in the exact market where Plug was trying to reposition GenSure and Project Gateway. [Bloom 2023 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2024/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2023-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) [Bloom 2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx)

The technology distinction still mattered. Bloom’s solid-oxide platform was sold as always-on distributed generation, often fuelled by natural gas today and capable of hydrogen over time. Plug’s GenSure proposition remained closer to clean backup and bridge power integrated with a hydrogen supply strategy. In procurement terms, Bloom arrived as a proven distributed-generation vendor; Plug arrived as a company arguing that its hydrogen ecosystem could solve resilience, emissions and fuel supply in one step. That was a credible pitch, but a harder one to underwrite. [Bloom 2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) [November 2025 infrastructure release](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Plug-Power-to-Generate-Over-275-Million-Through-Monetization-of-Electricity-Rights-and-Operational-Efficiencies-Supports-Major-U-S--Data-Center-Build-Out/default.aspx)

Bloom also showed what commercial traction in the AI-power trade looked like when it was already embedded in reported results: not simply strategic language, but rapid revenue growth, improving margins and a backlog discussion centred on the same customer category Plug was still approaching through infrastructure monetisation and collaboration. [Bloom 2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) [Stream agreement](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Executes-132-5-Million-Definitive-Agreement-with-Stream-Data-Centers-as-First-Step-in-275-Million-Strategic-Infrastructure-Optimization-Initiative/default.aspx)

## FuelCell Energy: Smaller, but Still in the Stationary Conversation

FuelCell Energy sat in a narrower lane than Bloom, but it could not be dismissed as a rounding error. It reported revenue of $112.1 million for fiscal 2024 and $158.2 million for fiscal 2025, and by late 2025 it too was talking openly about data-centre opportunities. Its carbonate-based systems, generation contracts and utility-style project history made it a different business from Plug, yet the comparison mattered because both companies were trying to convince investors that stationary power could become a large commercial endpoint for hydrogen-era infrastructure. [FuelCell 2024 results](https://investor.fce.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2024/FuelCell-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2024-Results/default.aspx) [FuelCell 2025 results](https://investor.fce.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/FuelCell-Energy-Ends-FY2025-with-Revenue-Growth-and-a-Focus-on-Data-Center-Opportunities/default.aspx)

Where FuelCell differed most sharply was in emphasis. Its public narrative leaned toward generation assets, long-term service agreements and utility-style development; Plug’s stationary-power case was inseparable from hydrogen production, logistics and the wider ecosystem argument. The overlap was real, but the route to monetisation was not the same. [FuelCell 2025 results](https://investor.fce.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/FuelCell-Energy-Ends-FY2025-with-Revenue-Growth-and-a-Focus-on-Data-Center-Opportunities/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## Ballard: Different End Market, Shared Investor Bucket

Ballard Power Systems was less of an operating rival to Plug than the market often assumed. Ballard’s core exposure was heavy-duty mobility: buses, rail, marine and other transport applications. It reported full-year revenue of $69.7 million in 2024 and $99.4 million in 2025, still well below Plug’s scale. The businesses nevertheless tended to trade in the same investor basket because both were read as listed PEM fuel-cell pure-plays. That meant sentiment shocks in one hydrogen name often bled into the others even where the commercial overlap was thin. [Ballard 2024 results](https://www.ballard.com/press-release/ballard-reports-q4-2024-results/) [Ballard 2025 results](https://www.ballard.com/press-release/ballard-reports-q4-2025-and-full-year-results/)

The limited overlap was analytically important. Plug was not trying to win transit-bus drivetrains or marine propulsion systems in the way Ballard was, and Ballard was not building the integrated warehouse, fuelling and hydrogen-supply architecture that defined Plug’s legacy franchise. The shared hydrogen label obscured genuinely different commercial maps. [Ballard 2025 results](https://www.ballard.com/press-release/ballard-reports-q4-2025-and-full-year-results/) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

## Electrolysers and the Industrial-Gas Shadow

In electrolysers, Plug competed in a broader and more structurally difficult arena than the fuel-cell peer set alone suggested. The direct public-company comparison included specialists such as Nel and ITM, but the more consequential strategic contest was against larger industrial and energy incumbents that could pair project-development capital with engineering depth. Plug’s differentiation was not that it had the only PEM-electrolyser platform; it was that it paired electrolysers with end-use fuel-cell demand, hydrogen logistics and company-owned production assets. [United Hydrogen and Giner ELX](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2020/Plug-Power-Inc.-Completes-Acquisitions-of-United-Hydrogen-and-Giner-ELX-continuing-to-execute-on-its-five-year-plan-2020-6-23/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

Looming behind the specialist peers were industrial-gas and engineering incumbents that could compete for the same sites, molecules and customers without depending on a single equity story. Plug’s owned plants in Georgia, Tennessee and Louisiana gave it a more tangible operating footprint than many pure-play peers could claim. They did not, however, free the company from competing against much stronger balance sheets. [Georgia start-up](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2024/Plug-Power-Starts-Production-of-Liquid-Green-Hydrogen-at-its-Georgia-Plant/default.aspx) [Louisiana commissioning](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/Hidrogenii-a-Plug-and-Olin-Joint-VentureCommissions-15-Ton-Per-Day-Hydrogen-Liquefaction-Plant-in-Louisiana/default.aspx) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.ir.plugpower.com/press-releases/news-details/2026/Plug-Power-Reports-Strong-Q1-2026-Results-with-22-Revenue-Growth-and-71-Margin-Improvement-Year-over-Year/default.aspx)

| Company | Reported scale point in latest referenced disclosure |
